Playbook.name: Windows — Kernel Driver (.sys) Created in a System Directory - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A .sys kernel-driver file was created in a system directory (FIM). Attackers drop malicious/vulnerable drivers (BYOVD) for kernel-level code execution and rootkit persistence. Triage: a legitimate driver install, or a malicious/vulnerable driver being planted?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A malicious or vulnerable kernel driver gives kernel-level (ring-0) code execution - defeating most endpoint defenses.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows FIM (verified live; monitors Windows system paths). Fields: file.path, file.name, file.extension, event.action, host.name.

Signal.Name: Kernel Driver (.sys) Created in a System

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the driver was created.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the kernel-driver file is a legitimate install or a malicious/vulnerable driver being planted.

Step.name: The driver file and creation context
Step.Purpose: The driver path/name and whether it accompanies a legitimate install separate benign from BYOVD/rootkit.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE event.dataset == "fim.event" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action == "created" AND file.extension RLIKE "(?i)sys" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, file.path, file.name, event.action | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A .sys with a random/unusual name in System32\drivers, not part of a signed software/driver install, is suspicious (possible BYOVD or rootkit). A driver dropped by a known installer/Windows Update is benign. Verify the driver's signature/reputation on the host.

Step.name: Was a service then created for the driver
Step.Purpose: A kernel-mode service registered for the new driver confirms it is being loaded.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.system-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "7045" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ImagePath, winlog.event_data.ServiceType | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A kernel-mode (ServiceType kernel) service pointing at the new .sys confirms the driver is being loaded - if the driver is unsigned/vulnerable, this is BYOVD - escalate.

Node.Condition: A random/unsigned .sys planted and loaded as a kernel service, not from a known install.
A driver installed by a signed software installer / Windows Update.
A legitimate but unusual driver install without a change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FIM-DRIVER, INV-02-FIM-DRIVERSVC to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the install; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host; open IR; remove the driver/service; check for kernel tampering; hunt the driver hash estate-wide.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Verify the driver's signature/reputation on the host; if malicious, isolate.
Check for a kernel service loading it.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; remove the driver/service; check for kernel tampering; hunt the hash.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable HVCI/driver blocklist (BYOVD protection); enforce driver signing; alert on new drivers.

QualityChecks.Check: fim.event monitors Windows paths; correlate with 7045 for kernel-service loading.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Malicious driver removed; kernel integrity checked; hash hunted.
